title: A deciding command's nonzero return masked by an unconditional true
purpose: Prevent a real failure being silently erased by following the deciding command with `; true`, a blanket default, or `|| true` on the wrong (value-deciding) command instead of on an incidental cleanup.
trigger: A command whose success/failure determines the result is immediately followed by a construct that forces a true/zero status (`; true`, `|| true`, returning a default) rather than propagating/branching on its code.
correct: Branch on the compound status or capture/read the code and decode it; reserve `|| true` strictly for incidental loggers/cleanup so they cannot add a nonzero, and never on the command that owns the outcome.
evidence_note: Grounded in queuebash.sh, which keeps the worker decision code by reading rc after wait and uses || true only on incidental loggers; docs/IPC.md propagates an external helper with || exit $?.
return_semantics: A reference rule page; shown for LLM author guidance, not executed by rules check.
